Detection Categories

Fine-tune the individual classes of sensitive data scanned by Privacy Shield.

CREDENTIALS & TOKENS
Password Fields Protected by input type and semantics without inspecting raw values
API Keys & Developer Secrets OpenAI, AWS, GitHub PATs, Slack, Stripe, and Google API keys
Authentication Tokens & JWTs JSON Web Tokens (Bearer eyJ...), session auth headers
OTPs & 2FA Codes One-time passcodes, verification codes with contextual keyword proximity
FINANCIAL & PERSONAL DATA
Credit & Debit Cards Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover with Mod 10 Luhn checksum validation
Bank Accounts & IBANs International Bank Account Numbers (Mod 97 check) & routing numbers
Email Addresses RFC 5322 pattern with file extension & TLD false-positive rejection
Phone Numbers International E.164 and localized numbers filtered against dates & IPs
Personal Addresses & SSN Social Security Numbers & physical street address designations

Security & Privacy Architecture

Complete audit overview of Privacy Shield's local-first privacy commitments.

100% On-Device Local Processing

Every detection routine, regular expression, and DOM scan runs strictly inside your local browser JavaScript engine. No content or keystrokes ever leave your computer.

Zero Telemetry, Tracking, or Remote JavaScript

Privacy Shield does not use Google Analytics, Sentry, external CDNs, or remote API endpoints. All fonts (Geist & Manrope) and icons are bundled locally inside the extension archive.

Password Value Protection

Privacy Shield never accesses, inspects, or logs the actual raw value of password input elements. It identifies the field via DOM attributes and applies visual protection directly to the rendered element.

Security Scope & Technical Limitations

Visual blurring is designed for screen-privacy against shoulder surfing, screen-sharing, recording, and accidental visual disclosure. It modifies visual presentation via CSS. It does not prevent malicious website scripts, other privileged browser extensions, DevTools DOM inspection, or low-level OS screen capture tools from reading underlying webpage memory.
